messages:
sarah: Hi team — AcmeLabs onboarding hit a bunch of 429s right after they swapped test->prod key. They say it started ~an hour ago in sandbox and is blocking demo tomorrow. Anyone free to triage?

matt: on it. can you paste the exact error payload and which SDK/version they're using?

sarah: paste: `Error: 429 Too Many Requests
  at request (/app/node_modules/redwood-sdk/index.js:123)
  retry-after: 21`
  They are on node-sdk v2.1.0, using our JS client inside a serverless function (Vercel).

devex-bot: quick check — common patterns: 1) long concurrency in serverless causing concurrent bursts, 2) key scoped to limited endpoints, 3) hitting account-level sandbox quota.

matt: looks like Retry-After returned 21s which suggests hitting per-minute RPM. sarah — can you confirm headers for one failing response?

sarah: headers: `retry-after: 21`, `x-rw-ratelimit-limit: 120`, `x-rw-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, `x-rw-ratelimit-reset: 167`

leo: that x-rw-ratelimit-limit=120 is per-minute for their org sandbox token. if they burst from serverless cold starts they'll hit this quickly. we recently put a conservative quota on sandbox orgs for new customers.

matt: two things to try: 1) throttle concurrency in their app to ~2 parallel requests, 2) implement exponential backoff honoring Retry-After. example backoff snippet:```js
// pseudo
await callApi();
if (resp.status === 429) {
  const wait = parseInt(resp.headers['retry-after'] || '1') * 1000;
  await sleep(wait + Math.random()*300);
  retry();
}
```

hana: flagging as onboarding blocker & potential renewal risk if demo fails. Sarah, please schedule an enablement call and include this troubleshooting checklist: key rotation permissions, concurrency limits, and whether they need a temporary RPM bump.

sarah: scheduled call for tomorrow 2pm PT, invite sent. Also discovered their onboarding script referenced `https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` instead of `https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/generate` — that caused the SDK to fall back to a legacy routing path which can behave differently under quotas. asked them to verify endpoint.

matt: good catch. endpoint mismatch can map requests to different quota buckets. if they can't rotate keys (they said internal policy prevents rotation), workaround: create a small proxy in their infra to queue/batch requests and smooth bursts. alternatively we can temporarily increase their RPM. @billing-bot can you assist?

billing-bot: ticket created Q-7892 for temporary quota bump request. Provisionally approved for 48h trial while onboarding. Ops SLA ETA 24h.

leo: i'll add a quick server-side guard we can toggle: return `x-rw-rate-limit-reset-ms` so SDKs can parse definitive ms reset. short-term, have them parse both `retry-after` and `x-rw-ratelimit-reset`.

matt: also recommend they set SDK max concurrency env var: `REDWOOD_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2` inside their serverless function. if they must keep higher concurrency, use local token sharding or dedicated capacity plan.

sarah: client agreed to proxy workaround for now and accepted the 48h bump. prepping pre-call doc + steps to rotate key post-demo. tagging this thread to follow up after the call. :thumbsup:

hana: thanks — please update the renewal risk tracker if demo shows improvement, otherwise we'll escalate to solutions engineering for Dedicated capacity recommendation.

sarah: will update after call, marking as monitoring until then.
